chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abdullah ibn Maymun, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them all). He said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) stipulated upon the neighbours of the mosque that they must attend the congregational prayer. And he said: Groups of people who do not attend the prayers must certainly desist, or I shall command a mu'adhin to call the adhan and then make the iqama, then command a man from my household — and he is Ali — to burn their homes with bundles of firewood, because they do not come to the prayer.

key_terms.اشترط: Stipulated, made as a condition — indicating a binding obligation placed on mosque neighbours
key_terms.المؤذن: The mu'adhin — the one who calls the adhan to prayer
key_terms.جيران المسجد: Neighbours of the mosque — those living close enough that the call to prayer (adhan) reaches them
key_terms.حزم الحطب: Bundles of firewood — the means by which the threat of burning was to be carried out
key_terms.شهود الصلاة: Attending/witnessing the prayer — presence at the congregational prayer in the mosque

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about neighbours of the mosque who miss congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith records the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) strong warning about neglecting congregational prayer for those living near a mosque. The Prophet stipulated attendance as a binding obligation for mosque neighbours and threatened that Imam Ali (AS) would burn the homes of persistent absentees — a severe rhetorical warning conveying the gravity of abandoning communal worship. The Imam's chain traces through al-Sadiq (AS) and his forefathers back to the Prophet, giving this narration strong Shia authority.
